name: Spring 2026

reviewed.titleEN: Nippon Sangoku: The Three Nations of the Crimson Sun
reviewed.titleJP: 日本三國
reviewed.review: I really hate it when there's a cool show on Amazon, because I refuse to pay for their no-ads option and their ads suck. But OK, this show is actually pretty cool from the start — really some cool direction and artistic choices. It's got a premise that gets into it and tells you what it's gonna be, from the title and then from everything else, and I'm curious to see if it's a show whose content matches up with my interest in the stylistic elements of it. So yeah, definitely gonna finish this episode.

fullReview.review: The show definitely has a cool visual vibe to it and good production values, but the first episode is just too dark and brutal, and I don't need that right now, so I'm gonna pass on it. But it is a cool premise, and I think a lot of it is well done. There's a lot of rotoscoping-type work in it, well done, just not something I want to dedicate my time to right now.

reviewed.titleJP: 神の庭付き楠木邸
reviewed.review: This appears to be another show in the calm, cozy slice-of-life genre, with a god that looks like Okami. The show seems fine, but that's about all. I don't have any particularly strong feelings for or against this show, which means I'm not gonna keep watching it — but if you watch it, that's totally fine too. Seems like it'll be a pleasant thing to watch in 2026.

reviewed.titleJP: 妄想代理人 [original broadcast: winter 2004]
reviewed.review: Dammit, this is still great. It still actually looks really good, which is especially hard considering the era it was made in, which was the early digital transition — there are a lot of things from that era that end up looking pretty trashy. Fabulous opening, too. It's a great episode, a great piece of Kon's work. And it's always interesting to see someone who primarily works in one medium translate to another — in this case, a film director going and doing a 13-episode TV series. So I'm very happy that we're watching/reviewing this again, and I'm definitely looking forward to seeing where this crazy show goes, one I haven't watched in over 20 years.

reviewed.titleEN: Hokuto no Ken: Fist of the North Star
reviewed.titleJP: 北斗の拳
reviewed.review: So this is a new version of this with very shaded 3D CGI. I'm not sure — I mean, frankly, I never really got into it the first time it started, but it's got that 80s Mad Max vibe to it, and the world is cruel and real. I can see why it's been popular for so long, as far as that goes. I'm really not sure — it definitely makes me want to go back and watch the original TV series. The only thing I could say is maybe the new version has some better plotting, or they'll at least have a shorter number of episodes to go through, but I don't know if that actually improves anything, so I'll give it a solid meh — finishing the ep, but that's about it.

reviewed.titleJP: スノウボールアース
reviewed.review: Well, I think this show is pretty great. They actually had a small pre-opening segment, but it actually made sense and was a bit of background exposition. The opening was good. The show definitely gives me some Giant Robo vibes, and there's kaiju, and they look ridiculous, which is great — so yeah, the first part of it is cool. They do a time skip after five minutes to like ten years later, so I'm curious if it's gonna stay good, but if that's the case, the show has a high chance of being actually pretty cool. So that's my hope.

fullReview.review: This is a pretty cool premise and well done. I've liked where it's continued to go from the first little bit that I watched. It definitely has an interesting mix of 2D and 3D stuff, leaning more into the 3D, which I can completely understand why they would've done. I'm curious where the story and all the work is gonna go, but it's pretty well done, and I like it — I find the characters genuinely engaging. It's got a cool world and idea of things there, and I feel like there's more to explore. Hopefully it continues to be good; I'm only a couple episodes in and it seems that way so far.

reviewed.titleJP: 淡島百景
reviewed.review: It's a really nicely done show about girls at a high school that appears to have some sort of special focus, but within the first six minutes or so, I still don't really know what type of school it is — whether it's a general one or not — but it's definitely a boarding school. Madhouse did the production, and it looks really nice. It's got a good look to it, very distinct and watercolor-looking, in a good way. It's a slow-moving show, but I'm curious to see where it goes.

fullReview.review: This is another very well-done show. I think it's gonna be a compilation of stories about different girls at an artistic high school, focusing around one at a time. Very nice production, well done overall, so it's a good show. I just don't think it's something I'm super interested in watching right now, but I could be convinced otherwise, and I could see other people being really into the show, 'cause it looks like it could actually be pretty good.

reviewed.titleJP: あかね噺
reviewed.review: Like the last review, this show's primary streaming source is also YouTube. However, this one is much easier to find the official version of, I guess, which is fine. As far as the anime goes — I'd read a little bit of the manga and didn't really take to it, I don't know for whatever reason, but I like the anime. It feels like it's got good production quality and flow to it. I'm already fairly interested in the main character, so we'll see where it goes from there, but yeah, I'm curious to see. I think probably the hardest part is just the content of this, which is that it's about a very old-style Japanese storytelling comedic thing that makes it very hard to get a good translation of. So I think that's gonna be the most challenging part of the whole thing, just seeing how they do all of that work. Hopefully they do their best with it and the material shows through.

fullReview.review: This has been one of my biggest surprise shows of the season. I started trying to read the manga a while ago, and I just didn't quite get into it. But this anime version is fabulous. They've done such a great job taking the story, and taking rakugo — which is such a weird, very Japanese thing, a subculture even over there — and made it into this really cool drama with interesting, good characters. The production values are just great throughout; clearly it's a show that's been done with a lot of care. So I'm very happy and surprised that it's been such a great show. I'm only a few eps in now, but I'm definitely gonna keep watching through the end of the season. It's really cool to see some of these things and learn a bit about another piece of Japanese culture — another art form that I've heard of but don't really know anything about. So in that way it's kind of like a sports anime, in that you really get to learn the details of this art form, which has kind of a competition but kind of not, and how that works. It's very well done.

reviewed.titleJP: 魔法の姉妹ルルットリリィ
reviewed.review: For one, this is streaming on the official platform of YouTube, which is weird, and I don't really like that, because YouTube doesn't have good subtitle support, and it can get really weird trying to actually find the thing you're looking for there, 'cause there's so many people ripping and re-uploading it. Anyway, it is streaming up there and there are subtitles. The show itself seems to be a cool new magical girl show from Studio Pierrot, so there's quite the pedigree there — a.k.a. the most pedigree for magical girl shows ever. The show itself looks to have pretty nice production values. The main characters definitely stand out, very nicely colored in bright pastels versus everyone else, who are a lot more muted. Good backgrounds, everything in there. I haven't quite gotten to the magical girl hook yet in the show, but it's gonna be a magical girl show from Studio Pierrot. The episode at least starts with the opening, which has weird lyrics, but you know, it's cool, and we'll see. I'll probably finish watching the episode to at least see the hook of it and see if it's good. Definitely weird having this streaming on YouTube as the primary platform.

fullReview.review: I never went back to the show, and I'm OK with that. I've got enough things to watch, and it's not the sort of thing that's called me back and forced me to check it out, particularly because I don't generally watch continuing longer-form stuff on YouTube. But it's better that it's on YouTube than on Amazon or HiDive.

reviewed.titleEN: Haibara-kun no Tsuyokute Seishun New Game
reviewed.titleJP: 灰原くんの強くて青春ニューゲーム
reviewed.review: So some sad-sack mid-20s guy decides he wants to really relive his high school years and become a high school superstar. So it's glory days, and it's pretty pathetic. That's what he wants to relive and redo, and there's a show about it, because that means there's probably a bunch of people who want to redo that too. The show itself is fine, production seems all right. I don't despise the main character yet or anything, so it's OK, that's all.

reviewed.titleJP: また殺されてしまったのですね、探偵様
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: The show tries to start out with some sort of hard-boiled detective thing, but then immediately gives that up in the opening, in a scene where you've got a big-breasted lady naked in the shower, and all sorts of other ladies in various outfits in the OP. So this is gonna be some sort of trashy harem detective show. Let's continue for another three minutes… so there is absolutely no reason to continue watching for the next three minutes. Nothing happened that changed anything. It's terrible. Don't watch it.

reviewed.titleJP: 神の雫
reviewed.review:
Oh damn, he's decanting like a professional! Even though he doesn't know anything about wine — oh man, this is so moving, so very wine, so very wine!
In a world where a wine critic's passing is front-page news on the big screens out in Tokyo, you've got the world of Drops of God.
So we finally have a sommelier show — it's gonna be completely ridiculous. Not quite sure exactly where it's going, but there's definitely gonna be some sommelier competition, and it's probably gonna be pretty dumb, but I might end up watching it just 'cause sometimes those shows are fun.

reviewed.titleEN: Kujima: Why Sing, When You Can Warble?
reviewed.titleJP: クジマ歌えば家ほろろ
reviewed.review: This is definitely one of those slice-of-life shows, but this one's based around some sort of weird bird-human creature in Japan, and a high schooler says the bird is committing a crime by finding 20 cents underneath a vending machine. It's probably fine, I'm not gonna watch it, though — I don't see anything here. But if you want something with some sort of bird slice-of-life, then… bird up, yo.

reviewed.titleJP: MAO (マオ)
reviewed.review:
Whoa, Sunrise, what?!?! Subs on Hulu are annoying because they don't actually do the right work, and they put them right on top of the on-screen captions introducing characters.
OK, so I'm gonna finish watching this episode because it's Rumiko Takahashi, and I love her stuff so much that there's no way I'm not at least watching a full episode. That said, as far as the first five minutes of the show go, it seems pretty good — I'm curious. It's very Takahashi: high school/middle school girl, and the opening shows some sort of demon things, so I definitely get, without knowing anything about it, some Inuyasha vibes, and that's fine. I'm OK with some Inuyasha vibes. So I'm curious to see where it goes. Overall production, everything looks pretty good — nothing that's unexpected or really out there, which I think is probably the right thing to do for a Takahashi show.

fullReview.review: This ended up being a great Rumiko Takahashi show. I really like the setting, the characters, the animation style — it's just very well done. It definitely has some of the feel of Inuyasha, but done differently, with a different relationship between now and the main female lead. There's a lot of interesting scenarios and drama that happens, and some interesting stuff with the timeline, because it's going back to the Taisho era — so it's not going back to a time that's before anything recognizable now. I think that makes it very interesting, in that it's kind of historical fiction but adding in more fantastical elements, while also being a world you can recognize and comprehend even while being a while ago. So I've definitely enjoyed it and will keep watching the full season.

reviewed.titleJP: だんでらいおん
reviewed.review: Netflix series, it's OK, that's fine. It's a dead-detectives-try-to-free-souls show, got some reasonable comedic stuff, some others. I'm not quite sure where it's going — could either go super serious or continue to lean more into the comedic stuff. It's fine, it's nothing. I'm probably gonna keep watching.

reviewed.titleEN: The Food Diary of Miss Maid
reviewed.titleJP: メイドさんは食べるだけ
reviewed.review: OK, so the show's trash, strictly second-screen viewing, that's it. Now, it's not offensive, it's like another touring show. This one's about a maid who's back in Japan, apparently for the first time since she was a child, but she shows up on day one dressed in her maid outfit, already cleaning, with a perfect understanding and comprehension of not only the Japanese language, but also every single Japanese cultural thing. The only thing she's missing is the experience of all the different food items across Tokyo, Japan, I guess. So it's a pretty dumb opening. I like the song, the animation was — again, not bad, just nothing that made me say "oh man, I gotta check this out." I do appreciate at least that they had the guts to actually start the show with the opening animation, rather than holding it back for the first episode for no reason other than not having the guts to put it at the beginning of your show because you don't think it's worthwhile, or whatever. So, it's trash, for second-screen viewing only. It's fine if you wanna watch a show that talks about a bit of food stuff and goes around showing different places with some sort of cute maid — then go for it, I do not judge thee.

reviewed.titleEN: The Classroom of a Black Cat and a Witch
reviewed.titleJP: 黒猫と魔女の教室
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: Truly just awful, bottom-of-the-barrel bad magic school show, with panties and girls asking other girls to pay with their bodies. It's not pornography, but it's just bad. There's no reason for this to exist, ever, for anyone. I just wanna not exist if this is what has to exist. It's not the worst show that's ever been made, but I wish it was never made.

reviewed.titleJP: ゴーストコンサート: missing Songs
reviewed.review: I feel like on the surface I should like this show, but I'm like eight minutes in and not really caring that much about anything that goes on with this. It's an idol singing show — the intro song, not the opening, was pretty nice, good song execution, all that stuff. It's set in the future, and I guess in the future they don't have the time to really put enough effort into the 3D work that they do — there's a lot of city and cars moving and all of these other bits, and it feels very un-cleaned-up and unfinished. So the show could maybe be cool, but I'm probably not gonna find out.

reviewed.titleEN: Botan Kamiina Fully Blossoms When Drunk
reviewed.titleJP: 上伊那ぼたん、酔へる姿は百合の花
reviewed.review: The production and everything of this is quite nice, well executed, good backgrounds, all those things, and the opening is pretty cool. I'm not quite sure how I feel about the actual show, because it seems like the premise is: a girl who's never had anything to drink before just starts downing highballs like it's nothing, and is then also immediately drunk from having those. It seems like it's gonna be one of those cute-girls-in-a-group shows, and the focus of this one, rather than music or sports or anything else, is drinking and smoking. So, you know… bottoms up!

reviewed.titleJP: リラックマ
reviewed.review: I wasn't sure if this was actually a real show or if it was season 85 of something, but it's a series of minute-and-a-half-long shorts done by Production I.G, and it's very charming, has a continuing story, and is a nice, refreshing thing to have in the year of our Lord 2026. So yeah, I recommend it if you want a nice, refreshing, silly thing to watch with a very catchy ending song.

ed.review: This ending has stuck with me through thick and thin. The song is so catchy, it's literally a third of the episode length because they're in love with the ending, and I just wanna watch more just so I can hear the ending song, 'cause it's so damn catchy.

reviewed.titleEN: The Strongest Job is Apparently Not a Hero or a Sage, but an Appraiser (Provisional)!
reviewed.titleJP: 最強の職業は勇者でも賢者でもなく鑑定士（仮）らしいですよ？
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: Oh my God, wow, this show's just terrible. I guess their redeeming quality — here it is, from the shows I've watched thus far — is that it's the first pure video-game isekai thing I've seen this season. We've already had the guy who doesn't know everything about his own classes, blah blah blah, and the elf girl with the ridiculously large boobs, whose buttons have already exploded as a plot device, which was then also shown in the opening. So, it's gonna be awful. Definitely do not watch.

reviewed.titleEN: An Observation Log of My Fiancée Who Calls Herself a Villainess
reviewed.titleJP: 自称悪役令嬢な婚約者の観察記録。
reviewed.review: This is definitely trash, for second-screen viewing only. The premise, I guess, is that the prince is a super-genius kid, and I can't tell if the heroine or a secondary character was reincarnated as the villainess. The production values actually seem fairly good; the part I find really weird is that there's this multi-layered overlay where you get the prince talking out loud, and then you get his internal voice in his head, but then there are other people whose internal monologues come off like a joke, but he can kind of hear it, and then there are also textual overlays like it's a video game, because it's supposed to kind of be a video game, I guess. But it's just too many of these devices.

reviewed.titleJP: NEEDY GIRL OVERDOSE
reviewed.review: Well, at least I'm raising my brow in curiosity about what the show is gonna be. So I don't have the highest hopes, but I'm always curious. It's got some interesting stuff going on — it's an idol show, but it also looks like it's kind of trying to be a social-commentary type show about social media overload. I like some of the stylistic choices, and some others look a little weird, like mobile-game-style 3D anime girl stuff, and then other parts are very vaporwave-looking. So I'm curious to at least see the end of the episode.

fullReview.review: The show got really weird and stayed very weird. It has kind of a Bakemonogatari style to it, but much less dialogue-driven, and leans more into monologue, trying to make a million statements about modern social media culture. I'm very confused by it. Some of the art choices and stuff are cool, but it's so disjointed and out there that it's not clear to me what they're going for. There was more I thought about after this, but it wasn't boring, and the opening, which played at the end of the episode, is pretty cool, very well done.

reviewed.titleJP: カナン様はあくまでチョロい
reviewed.review: You know what you're getting into within the first ten seconds of this — it's a very fine example of trash, strictly second-screen viewing. I'm not gonna keep watching. It is trash, and it is only fit for the second screen.

reviewed.titleJP: 氷の城壁
reviewed.review: Another high school show — seems like maybe that's a new thing to do a lot of, rather than isekai. I'm fine with this, prefer it. This side commentary is now over. The show is pretty good, it's fine, it's got good production values, good overall feel to it. Nothing that seems bad, it's not the best thing I've seen, but it seems OK. So — that was a very noncommittal review, but I guess that sums up how I feel about this, in too many words.

reviewed.titleJP: 逃がした魚は大きかったが釣りあげた魚が大きすぎた件
reviewed.review:
Thirty seconds in, and it literally just aped the beginning of the much more fun "Excuse Me While I Finally Punch You in the Face" show.
I guess it's OK, I don't know — again, nothing that's really worth anyone's time to watch or produce, so, blah.

reviewed.titleJP: ニワトリ・ファイター
reviewed.review: I was aware of the manga for this for a while, but I never got into reading it. The adaptation here, without knowing that, is pretty good. I'm not quite sure I love that all the monsters look to be a 3D thing, but at least it looks nice, and that's fine. I like the voices, the overall feel — it's got a good kind of One Punch Man vibe to it, so this one's definitely got potential to be a pretty fun show.

fullReview.review: Overall, this was really fun. It's a pretty ridiculous mashup of demon fighting — almost Fist of the North Star meets Dragon Ball, but with a rooster. Looks like there's gonna be a rooster team that's the only one capable of stopping demons, and humans are completely worthless. It's a pretty funny premise. I'm not sure if I'm gonna keep watching it. I like the pacing. The animation is very CG-based; it looks pretty consistent at least, and well styled. I'm not sure I love everything about it, but I can see why they did that — it lets them do some cool stuff with the demons, I think, without breaking style. But it leads to some of the characters looking very weird, though that might also just be consistent with the original manga source.

reviewed.titleJP: ライアーゲーム
reviewed.review: I was very hopeful for this show, because I love a good death-game/battle-royale-type show, and the first five minutes of this look pretty good. I'm definitely in on it, so here's hoping it ends up being cool.

fullReview.review: Liar Game is pretty fun. It's not my favorite thing ever, partially, I think, because the main character remains so clueless but keeps surviving anyway. But it's plainly done. It's got a Eurobeat-style opening, which always helps me, and it's a fun, ridiculous game of debt and betting and lying and everything — and it is the Liar Game. So if you're interested in any show that's called Liar Game and is a game about lying, then I definitely recommend it, it's pretty good.

reviewed.titleEN: I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class
reviewed.titleJP: クラスで2番目に可愛い女の子と友だちになった
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review:
Two minutes in and I got through the opening. There's a red balloon in it that I thought got away, and I felt like, man, I really wish I could be that red balloon and escape — but then it was trapped and grabbed by the completely pointless main character in their stupid love-triangle thing, and their good friend who does the arm-around-the-neck thing in the opening. So now I've got another three minutes left before I get my life back.
Somehow it got even more boring, and there's still thirty seconds left. Oh God, I will survive.

reviewed.titleJP: ただいま、お邪魔させます！
reviewed.review: It's fine, I guess it's not my type of show. I think it's gonna be a… I don't know, I don't really care, so I guess that's where I'm at. I just don't care. It's fine.

reviewed.titleEN: I Want to End this Love Game
reviewed.titleJP: 愛してるゲームを終わらせたい
reviewed.ratingText: I want to end this review
reviewed.review: No. It's not great. I think there's a manga this comes from — maybe it's more fun there, but this is just blah, and not particularly excellently executed or anything to make up for it. So, no thanks, I'm out.

reviewed.titleEN: Even a Replica Can Fall in Love
reviewed.titleJP: レプリカだって、恋をする。
reviewed.review: Even a replica deserves to not have to watch this show. Oh my God, so boring, so nothing, just... nothing. I'd rather be the main character, who is in bed not participating in it. OK, done.

reviewed.titleEN: The Klutzy Class Monitor and the Girl with the Short Skirt
reviewed.titleJP: ポンコツ風紀委員とスカート丈が不適切なJKの話
reviewed.review: The show is actually OK. I'm sure it's gonna be awful at some level, but it at least has some really cool color choices, and some decent direction in it. I found some of it to be kind of funny and well executed, so it was definitely better than I was hoping it was going to be. Am I gonna keep watching it? Probably not, but it's not the worst thing I've seen.

reviewed.titleJP: キルアオ
reviewed.review: I like the background art — the direction has some interesting composition in there. Other than that, it's a hard-boiled-assassin-gets-reincarnated-into-a-younger-body thing, so it's dumb. I'm not gonna watch any more of it, but I guess it's OK.

reviewed.titleEN: Agents of the Four Seasons: Dance of Spring
reviewed.titleJP: 春夏秋冬代行者 春の舞
reviewed.review: I wasn't in on the show for the first minute or so, but then it got a little bit interesting with the plot and world. I'm still not quite sure on the characters or where it's gonna go. Production values are good. I'm kind of curious about this one.

reviewed.titleJP: ガンバレ！中村くん!!
reviewed.review: So this might actually be a decent school-romance, rom-com thing. The art style is very reminiscent of Here Is Greenwood, in the best way, because that's a brilliant art style, and it features a guy who's got a crush on another guy, and it's being done in a very normal way, not for any sort of weird thrills or anything, at this point. So I'm definitely curious to see where it goes.

fullReview.review: I finished the first two episodes of this show, and it's great. It really delivers on everything I was hoping it would, which is that it's a charming, awkward romantic comedy that's very well executed, with a consistent art style and perspective throughout. I'm very much looking forward to seeing more, and I hope the story stays good and fun and interesting, because I like what they've started out with, and I'm really hoping it continues through the end of the season. I'm a sucker for Here Is Greenwood, and this is a show that reminds me of that in such a strong way, while not being a copy or anything related to it. It definitely gives me big vibes from that, in the best possible way.

reviewed.titleJP: 転生したらドラゴンの卵だった ～最強以外目指さねぇ～
reviewed.review: I feel like I literally watched this show last season. It did not get any better with time. Absolutely not worth anyone's time to create this, produce it, stream it, watch it, review it, or read the review of it.

reviewed.titleJP: 霧尾ファンクラブ
reviewed.review: OK, so this is actually pretty cool. At least it's got a chance. Fabulous OP. Very cool intro scene. I'm not sure where it's going, but it could be quite good. Aside — OMG, the audio on HiDive is so terrible. I'm watching downloaded on iPad via AirPods on a plane, and I can hear all the air/gaps/pops. Do better, man, do better.

fullReview.review: This episode was pretty good, and there's a little twist at the end of it, but this is a show I'm not gonna continue watching. It's fine, just not for me, so nothing here really changed my mind on that.

reviewed.titleEN: The Most Heretical Last Boss Queen: From Villainess to Savior Season 2
reviewed.titleJP: 悲劇の元凶となる最強外道ラスボス女王は民の為に尽くします。Season2
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: Apparently I watched this for five minutes. I want my life back.

reviewed.titleJP: よわよわ先生
reviewed.ratingText: I wish I never came back to this
reviewed.review: I stopped watching this on the plane because the intro got very uncomfortably ecchi. So I came back later on my own, and I wish I had just stopped watching and never picked it up again. It's awful in every way. Everything is bad. Bad, bad, bad, bad, bad, bad.

reviewed.titleJP: リィンカーネーションの花弁
reviewed.review: I'm kind of curious about this. I can't tell if it's gonna be cool or just totally fall apart by the end of the first episode. So I'll say "cool" and hope I'm right. It definitely gives me some *Monogatari vibes.

reviewed.titleJP: 俺のリブな転生記
reviewed.review: All right, first review of the season, with this show that had a title that was a little off-putting. But the actual show could be OK. It's got some really interesting animation and design/aesthetic choices. I can't tell anything about the actual story or characters at this point, but I don't hate it, and I'm kind of curious to see where it goes. So I'll take that as a positive sign for a random show that looks potentially terrible, but, you know, it could be OK.

fullReview.review: This was a show that I initially gave a "Meh" to, but it's actually pretty good. It's a whole bunch of differing, weird reincarnation stuff — however, the rules are pretty funny, in that, like, the main character says "I wanna be reincarnated as a cute toe," and the goddess says, "OK sure, you can do that, but there's a 500,000-year wait on getting reincarnated there." So then he negotiates and ends up with all these weird little things, like being reincarnated as the main heroine's rib, but somewhat sentient. It's very well done. It has a bunch of very cool, interesting animation, ranging from bits of straight-up 2D to very crayon-style to literally claymation, and some fun live-action stuff. I really like that at the end of the episode they show you how they made some of the cool segments, which I think adds to it, and it's pretty darn funny. They keep the various story jokes to two storylines per episode, so it's definitely been a very pleasantly pleasing show that I can recommend.

reviewed.titleJP: エレン・ザ・サウスポー
reviewed.review: The show's got me curious. Cool opening song, the animation is pretty decent. It's another one where I'm not quite sure where the story is going, but it's already done a couple of different little time-leaps back and forth, so I'm definitely curious. Doesn't hurt that Production I.G is involved in this, so that's a good sign for a quality show, I think. Plus, it features a lefty, so I'll take that as a win.

fullReview.review: Finished the first episode; it's fine, better than most of the things out there, and worth watching, or so. The thing I find off about it is that the main guy in the show is just such a turd of a teenager — and by that I mean someone who thinks so highly of himself and doesn't realize he's just kind of a turd. Plus, he's got a not-quite-girlfriend girlfriend who's clearly a much better organized, put-together human being, and she's willing to sink her ship as part of his flotilla — I don't know, bad analogy, but she's trying to tie herself to him, and I'm just like, oh my God, ditch that loser. OK, anyways, I'm probably not gonna watch much more than this, but that's OK. Update: watched the second episode, and the main character got to be even more insufferable, and others were just hurting, and it was just completely insufferable teenage-dirtbag nonsense, so I don't need that.

reviewed.titleJP: とんがり帽子のアトリエ
reviewed.review: Production values are nice, but honestly, I'm kind of bored. I'm not really sure where it's going. It could be a good show, but not enough to capture me here.

reviewed.titleJP: 黄泉のツガイ
reviewed.review: So this is new work from Studio Bones, and from the author of Fullmetal Alchemist. I never got into Fullmetal Alchemist, so I can't really say I'm already sold. But the initial part of it seems kind of interesting — I'm actually curious to see who's doing what, and where they're going with the world they've got set up. So I think it's got good potential to be cool. I'll probably finish watching the episode.

fullReview.review: Watched the first several episodes of the show, and it's pretty well done. It's a cool take, kind of mixing old and new stuff in a fantastical, magical world that's also kind of grounded in reality. I'm sure it's a fun show, but for me, there was also nothing that particularly made me say "oh man, I gotta watch the next episode." So I'll probably not watch the next episode.

reviewed.titleJP: マリッジトキシン
reviewed.review: It could be OK, I don't know. Character designs are decent, but I'm not committing myself to watching more of this. I think there's a manga this is from — I might be more interested to read the manga.
